content.text: a chef cooking over a gas stove

explanationText.text: Gas stoves run on natural gas or other fossil fuels. When these gases are burned, carbon dioxide, which is a greenhouse gas, is released into the air. So, cooking over a gas stove releases greenhouse gases.

content.text: a company operating a coal-fired power plant

explanationText.text: Coal is a fossil fuel. When coal is burned, carbon dioxide, which is a greenhouse gas, is released into the air. So, operating a coal-fired power plant releases greenhouse gases.

content.text: a person driving a gasoline-powered car

explanationText.text: Gasoline comes from oil, which is a fossil fuel. When gasoline is burned, carbon dioxide, which is a greenhouse gas, is released into the air. So, driving a gasoline-powered car releases greenhouse gases.

There are many natural sources of greenhouse gases, including respiration. When an animal breathes out during respiration, carbon dioxide is released into the air. Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas. So, breathing releases greenhouse gases.
